name: Marti Ke
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Tryon 1974 Daly Family Languages full text searched: Magati Ke/Marti Ke not covered; only unpublished field materials (I. Green) known.
earlier_scan.note: No published description covering stress located.

sources.citation: Bicevskis, Katie. 2023. A grammatical description of Marri Ngarr. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne. https://hdl.handle.net/11343/336965
sources.note: MARRI NGARR only (sec. 2.2.3 pp. 34-38, impressionistic): 'In nominals, primary stress occurs on the first syllable of the stem. Words with three or more syllables can attract secondary stress on the third syllable'; simple verbs stress the first syllable of the classifier stem, bipartite verbs the first syllable of the lexical stem. Says nothing about Magati Ke stress; Magati Ke appears only as the sister dialect (p. 9, 'considered to be a dialect with Magati Ke (Green and Nordlinger 2022)'), in the note that Tryon 1974 'doesn't document Magati Ke', and in sec. 2.1.3 p. 25 (Magati Ke has /l/…

sources.citation: Mansfield, John. 2022 (preprint). Word prominence in polysynthetic Australian languages. PsyArXiv 9wexr, sec. 5.4 'Other Daly languages'
sources.note: Generalisation, not Magati Ke data: Western Daly languages Marrithiyel, Marri Ngarr and Emmi 'have been described as having initial primary stress for all word types, and thus on the first syllable of the finite stem in verbs (Ford, 1998, p. 70ff.; Green, 1989, p. 36; Reid, 1990, p. 96)', with secondary stress on the coverb's initial syllable. Magati Ke not mentioned.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record mart1254 and reference 61434 (Nambatu et al. 2009). https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mart1254
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 0 descriptive references; MEDs all wordlist_or_less (Nambatu et al. 2009 ix+226 pp. lgcode 'Marti Ke [zmg], Maringarr [zmt]'; Tindale 1974; Falkenberg 1962); links to PHOIBLE mart1254, ELP 2330.

sources.citation: Green, Ian & Rachel Nordlinger. 2022-. The Daly Languages (Australia) website, Magati Ke page (id=11), Marri Ngarr page (id=12) and Resources page. https://www.dalylanguages.org/view_language.php?id=11
sources.note: Nothing. States Magati Ke 'has been almost invisible in the linguistic record. It is not mentioned in Tryon (1974), and Nambatu et al's (2009) work on plant and animal names is the only substantial published information available on the language'; Ian Green's holdings = 3 h of recordings with Jonny Chula (01/11/1990, IG3-001..003) plus field notes IG3-N01 with 'preliminary morphological analyses... only basic data'; 'dialects with: Marri Ngarr'; no longer spoken. Key published resources: Nambatu et al. 2009 only; no sketch or phonology served.

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. 2019. Phonemic inventories of Australia (database of 392 languages). In S. Moran & D. McCloy (eds), PHOIBLE 2.0: inventory 2640 'Marti Ke' (31 phonemes), source key nambatu_marri_2009. https://phoible.org/inventories/view/2640; https://github.com/phoible/dev/tree/master/raw-data/ER
sources.note: Phonemes only ('contain only phonemes, with no information on allophones or linguistic tone'); nothing on stress. Establishes that Nambatu et al. 2009 (Batchelor Press) is the source of the only published Magati Ke phoneme inventory.

sources.citation: Nordlinger, Rachel. 2017. The languages of the Daly River region (Northern Australia). In Fortescue, Mithun & Evans (eds), The Oxford Handbook of Polysynthesis, 782-807. OUP (accepted manuscript, hdl 11343/217027)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Magati Ke appears only in the Western Daly family table under Marri Ngarr.

sources.citation: Marett, Allan, Linda Barwick & Lysbeth Ford. 2013. For the sake of a song: Wangga songmen and their repertories. Sydney University Press (ch. 3 by Ford). https://open.sydneyuniversitypress.com.au/files/
sources.note: Nothing for Magati Ke: names it 'Marri Ngarr and its coastal dialect, Magati Ke' / 'Marri Ngarr and its dialect Magati Ke' (Green 1994 MS subgrouping); sound-system tables are Marri Tjavin-Marri Ammu and Emmi-Mendhe only; bibliography lists Ford, Kungul & Jongmin 2000 (sociolinguistic survey of Wadeye, TELS paper) and Green 1994 MS 'The Daly language family: a reassessment, Proto Western Daly'.

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 2003. The genetic status of Murrinh-patha. In Nicholas Evans (ed.), The Non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia: comparative studies of the continent's most linguistically complex region, 125-158. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 552. DOI 10.15144/PL-552.125
sources.note: Nothing for Marringarr/Matige. Uses 'Green (field notes 1990-94)' Marringarr data; p. 126: Murrinh-patha 'borders on the north with Marringarr (the Marringarr and Matige dialects)'; fn. 7 p. 128: 'The Western Daly subgroup consists of Marringarr (dialects Marringarr, Matige), Marrithiyel (...), Marramaninjsji and Marranj'. Comparative verb-auxiliary and pronoun morphology only; the chapter's stress remarks concern Ngan'gityemerri.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1974. Daly family languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32; Tryon 1968 The Daly River languages: a survey, PL A-14
sources.note: Zero hits for Magati/Matige/Magadige: Tryon did not record the language (confirmed by Bicevskis 2023 p. 9 and the Daly Languages site). No word-stress statement anywhere in either volume.

sources.citation: Batchelor Institute, Centre for Australian Languages and Linguistics (CALL) collection: Magati Ke and Marri Ngarr language pages; Wadeye Endangered Languages Project page. https://call.batchelor.edu.au/languages/magati-ke
sources.note: Nothing; no downloadable resources listed for Magati Ke (project description only).

sources.citation: Ford, Lysbeth. 2010. Marri Ngarr and Magati Ge Learner's Guide. Batchelor, NT: Batchelor Institute Press.

sources.note: Only known work with a pronunciation section that treats Magati Ke explicitly (Bicevskis 2023 pp. 15, 25 cite its p. 10 for Magati Ke laterals); a learner's guide pronunciation section is the most likely place for a Magati Ke stress remark. Not in the Batchelor Press online catalogue or CALL; no digital copy found.

In print only (Batchelor Press AUD 35; LANT catalogue record OCLC 647851526); not digitised on Territory Stories.
